### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Guttmacher syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:5102)

**Proposed mechanism:** HOXA13 (HGNC:5102) —DISRUPTS→ Vertebral and limb development pathway; Vertebral and limb development pathway —LEADS_TO→ Hand-foot-genital syndrome phenotypes; Vertebral and limb development pathway —LEADS_TO→ Guttmacher syndrome phenotypes. Haploinsufficiency of the HOXA13 gene disrupts critical developmental pathways, leading to the distinct but overlapping phenotypic features of Hand-foot-genital syndrome and Guttmacher syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in HOXA13 that exhibit gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, rather than haploinsufficiency, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: None specified for pathogenic HOXA13 variants in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in HOXA13 can inform diagnostic approaches and potentially identify common therapeutic targets for both Hand-foot-genital syndrome and Guttmacher syndrome, focusing on developmental pathway regulation.
